chapter: Recent years and early piano influences
title: Clarence Profit's harmonic style
summary: Profit played flatted fifths and ninth chords, between Fats and James P.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: How would you describe Clarence Profit's style at that time?
It was like between J.P. Johnson and Fats Waller. Only he was more inventive, and he used to... His harmonies.... He was noted for his harmonies, the way he

used to try(?) that. He had that thing about him that... He'd go into the ...(?)... things. Where Fats Waller and J.P. had a harmonic continuity, I mean a standard continuity of Blues, Clarence Profit would try... Well, I would say he was flatting fifths around that time. He would reach...he'd go into ninth chords, you know.
Well, James P. and Fats were both inventive pianists, but they were... It was really all in that Stride idiom. Is that what you mean?
Yeah, rhythmic stride piano. But at the same time, Fats and them, they were great composers...
